feedback: You discussed the difference between getting a result with AI and actually learning the underlying structure. You explained that heavy AI use can make your thinking feel shallower, but you also described a more balanced strategy: use AI as a starting point, then verify important information yourself. Your main recurring weakness was sentence construction under pressure, especially tense consistency, verb patterns, and restarting long ideas. Your strongest moments came when you reduced the idea to one clear sentence and then added the next point.

corrections.original: I try to build an AI secretary quickly but I stop analyzing it deeply because it felt beyond my skill level.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Keep the whole story in the past tense.
corrections.natural: I tried to build an AI secretary quickly, but I stopped analyzing the code deeply because it felt beyond my skill level.
corrections.reason: The experience already happened, so 'tried' and 'stopped' should match 'felt' in the past tense.

corrections.original: I don't feel AI is increased my coding skills.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Use 'using AI' as the subject and a verb that means 'make better.'
corrections.natural: I don't feel that using AI has improved my coding skills.
corrections.reason: 'Has improved' naturally describes whether a tool has made your skill better over time; 'is increased my skills' is not a valid verb structure.

corrections.original: I don't think more by using the AI model ... which make me think low, not deep.
corrections.selfCorrectionCue: Use a simple comparative adverb for depth of thinking.
corrections.natural: I feel that relying on AI makes me think less deeply and use my own reasoning less.
corrections.reason: 'Think less deeply' is the natural way to express shallow thinking, and 'makes' agrees with the singular idea 'relying on AI.'

lessonNote.finalVersion: I recently tried to build an AI secretary quickly using code. At first, AI made it easy to get something working, but I stopped analyzing the structure deeply because it felt beyond my skill level. That made me realize that getting a result is not the same as learning. When I rely on AI too much, I sometimes feel that I think less deeply and use my own reasoning less. Still, I don't reject AI. I use it as a starting point, especially when it shows me something I might have missed, but I don't trust the output completely. I verify important information myself because I've seen incorrect translations and other mistakes.
recallQuestions: Why didn't building the AI secretary make you feel that your coding skills had improved?
